Class WhoAdminAutoConfiguration

java.lang.Object
org.jwcarman.who.autoconfigure.WhoAdminAutoConfiguration
@AutoConfiguration(after={WhoAutoConfiguration.class,WhoSpringSecurityAutoConfiguration.class,WhoEmailLinkAutoConfiguration.class}) @EnableConfigurationProperties(WhoProperties.class) @ConditionalOnClass(name={"org.jwcarman.who.admin.WhoAdminEndpoints","org.jwcarman.who.rbac.RbacPermissionsResolver"}) @ConditionalOnBooleanProperty(name="who.admin.enabled", matchIfMissing=true) public class WhoAdminAutoConfiguration extends Object
Registers who's admin endpoints when who-admin is on the classpath, unless who.admin.enabled=false. With email sign-in on, they also find identities by address, and POST /invitations invites people through its InvitationService.

  • Method Details

    • whoLastAdminGuard

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean @ConditionalOnSingleCandidate(org.springframework.transaction.PlatformTransactionManager.class) public LastAdminGuard whoLastAdminGuard(org.springframework.jdbc.core.simple.JdbcClient jdbcClient, org.springframework.transaction.PlatformTransactionManager transactionManager, PermissionsResolver permissionsResolver)
      Keeps the admin endpoints from leaving no active identity that may manage identities. It counts who-rbac's role holders, so it enforces the rule only when the application's permissions come from who-rbac; with a PermissionsResolver of the application's own it refuses nothing, and says so at startup. It needs a single PlatformTransactionManager: without one the admin endpoints, which require it, fail startup rather than run without the rule.
      Parameters:
      jdbcClient - reads who-rbac's tables and takes the locks
      transactionManager - runs each count and change in one transaction
      permissionsResolver - the application's resolver, which says whether holders can be counted
      Returns:
      the guard

    • whoAdminEndpoints

      @Bean @ConditionalOnMissingBean public WhoAdminEndpoints whoAdminEndpoints(WhoPaths paths, IdentityRepository identityRepository, WhoService whoService, RbacService rbacService, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<IdentityEmails> emails, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<LastCredentialGuard> guard, LastAdminGuard lastAdmin, WhoSessionSecurityContextRepository sessionRepository, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<WhoExceptionHandoff> handoff, org.springframework.beans.factory.ObjectProvider<tools.jackson.databind.json.JsonMapper> jsonMapper, Clock clock, WhoProperties properties)
      The admin endpoints at /identities and /roles under who.base-path, on every browser chain and every stateless chain.
      Parameters:
      paths - where the endpoints live
      identityRepository - pages through and reads identities
      whoService - deactivates and reactivates identities
      rbacService - reads, assigns and removes roles
      emails - the identities' addresses, when email sign-in is on
      guard - counts each identity's sign-in credentials, if there is one
      lastAdmin - keeps the last identity that may manage identities
      sessionRepository - tells a browser session from a key or a token
      handoff - the application's exception handling, if it has who's handoff
      jsonMapper - the application's JSON mapper, if it has one
      clock - the current time
      properties - who.security.recent-sign-in
      Returns:
      the endpoints
